title: Access lists
intro: L3/L4 and MACIP access lists, their rules, and where they are attached. Edits go to the candidate configuration; commit them from the pending-change bar.

adl.text: Access-list based ADL / Auto-SDL is configured on the interface security settings.

readonly: Your role cannot change the configuration

counters.notInVpp: This rule is not in VPP (not committed, disabled or outside its schedule)

lists.deleteText_one: The list and its {{n}} rule are removed from the candidate.
lists.deleteText_other: The list and its {{n}} rules are removed from the candidate.
lists.deleteAttached_one: It is still attached once: remove the attachment too, or the commit fails validation.
lists.deleteAttached_other: It is still attached {{n}} times: remove the attachments too, or the commit fails validation.
lists.name: Name
lists.nameHelp: Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore; up to 63 characters
lists.exists: A list with this name exists already

rules.pickList: Choose a list to edit its rules.
rules.noLists: There are no access lists yet: create one on the Lists tab.
rules.dragHandle: Drag rule {{sequence}} onto another rule to place it before that rule
rules.searchHelp: Every word must match (address, object, port, description…)
rules.notApplied: This list is not in VPP: it is not committed, or not attached to any interface.

bulk.label: Bulk actions
bulk.deleteText: The rules are removed from the candidate; nothing changes in VPP until you commit.
bulk.moveHelp: The selected rules get this sequence and the following numbers, in their current order; rules already there move down.

renumber.title: Renumber the list
renumber.help: Every rule of the list gets a new sequence in its current order: start, start + step, …

rule.stale: This rule changed in the candidate since the page was read (another session moved or deleted rules). Refresh and edit it again.

import.title: Import rules into {{list}}
import.help: A CSV file with a header row, up to 100 000 rules (format: see the ACL user guide). A dry run checks it first; nothing is written until you import.
import.done: Imported {{imported}} rules; the list now has {{total}} rules in the candidate.
import.afterReplace: The {{existing}} current rules would be replaced; the list would have {{total}} rules.
import.afterAppend: Appended to the {{existing}} current rules; the list would have {{total}} rules.

attachments.removedPending_one: {{n}} attachment removed in the candidate (not committed).
attachments.removedPending_other: {{n}} attachments removed in the candidate (not committed).
attachments.deleteText: {{list}} is detached from {{target}} in the candidate.
attachments.liveHelp: ACLs bound to each interface as VPP holds them, in evaluation order. ACLs of other owners are kept and shown, never edited here.

macip.deleteText: The list is removed from the candidate.
macip.deleteAttached: The list is removed from the candidate. It is still attached: remove the attachment too, or the commit fails validation.
macip.attachmentsEmpty: No MACIP list is attached yet.
macip.attachHelp: MACIP lists filter incoming traffic by source MAC and IP address; an interface holds one MACIP list.
macip.deleteAttachmentText: {{list}} is detached from {{interface}} in the candidate.
macip.onePerInterface: {{interface}} already has a MACIP list: an interface holds only one.

entry.stale: The candidate changed since the table was read (another session). Nothing was saved: close, refresh and try again.

ipVersion.title: IP version
ipVersion.help: IPv4 + IPv6 matches both families; it must agree with the prefixes and the ICMP protocol

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.help: A schedule object; empty = always active

name.title: Object
name.help: An object or group from the Objects page

tcpFlags.title: TCP flags
tcpFlags.help: Optional, as JSON: {"mask": 18, "value": 2} matches SYN set with ACK clear; empty = any flags

mask.title: Mask
mask.help: Bit mask over the TCP flags (FIN … CWR)

code.title: ICMP code
code.help: needs a type; empty = any code

vrf.title: VRF
vrf.help: Must be the VRF of the target interface
